content:
According to the latest report from Bloomberg, Apple is less than two weeks away from unveiling a brand-new smart display. The report further reveals design details of the long-awaited smart home hub.

Bloomberg reports that the home hub will feature a 6-inch square display, with an overall design reminiscent of the classic iMac G4 — which was known back in the day for its hemispherical base paired with a metal arm supporting the screen.

Mark Gurman says the device is "roughly the same thickness as an iPhone," with bezels using a quarter-inch black design similar to older iPads. The body has rounded corners with "no sharp edges whatsoever."

Here are more design details mentioned in the report:

  • The body features Apple's "standard gray aluminum finish," with "a rubber material added to the bottom to prevent the device from slipping."
  • It comes with a single USB-C port for power, with no built-in battery, meaning it must be connected to a power source at all times.
  • The base features a "circular metal design with multiple rings of perforated speaker holes."
  • The display is connected to the base via a "polished metal arm."
  • Users can tilt the display forward and backward to adjust the angle.
  • There are no volume or power buttons on the device.
  • It features a single front-facing FaceTime camera, with no rear camera.

Bloomberg also revealed another version of the home hub, "designed for wall mounting." This version is also powered via USB-C and features a "slim square base below the screen with built-in speakers and microphones." The base is reported to "sit flush against the wall beneath the screen."

For the full report, you can head over to the Bloomberg website. What are your thoughts on Apple's home hub product? Are you planning to get one (or more)? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
